tool.name: testssl.sh
tool.description: Comprehensive TLS/SSL testing tool for validating endpoint security.

severity_filtering.description: Only show HIGH and CRITICAL findings

tool.automation_example:
#!/bin/bash # Automated TLS validation script
ENDPOINTS=( "https://api.example.com" "https://app.example.com" "https://admin.example.com" )
RESULTS_DIR="tls-scan-results" mkdir -p "$RESULTS_DIR"
for endpoint in "${ENDPOINTS[@]}"; do echo "Scanning $endpoint..." ./testssl.sh --jsonfile "$RESULTS_DIR/$(echo $endpoint | sed 's/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/_/g').json" \ --severity HIGH \ "$endpoint" done
# Parse results and check for failures python3 << 'EOF' import json import glob import sys
critical_found = False for file in glob.glob('tls-scan-results/*.json'): with open(file) as f: data = json.load(f) for finding in data.get('scanResult', []): if finding.get('severity') in ['CRITICAL', 'HIGH']: print(f"FAILURE: {finding['id']} - {finding['finding']}") critical_found = True
sys.exit(1 if critical_found else 0) EOF

best_practices.practice: Run testssl.sh after every deployment
Automate scanning with CI/CD integration
Store results for trend analysis
Alert on any HIGH or CRITICAL findings
Validate all public-facing TLS endpoints

tool.name: SSLyze
tool.description: Fast, Python-based TLS scanner with programmatic interface.
tool.programmatic_usage:
# Python script for automated TLS validation from sslyze import ( Scanner, ServerScanRequest, ServerNetworkLocation, ScanCommand ) import json
def scan_endpoint(hostname, port=443): # Create scanner scanner = Scanner()
# Define server to scan server_location = ServerNetworkLocation(hostname, port) scan_request = ServerScanRequest( server_location=server_location, scan_commands={ ScanCommand.CERTIFICATE_INFO, ScanCommand.TLS_1_2_CIPHER_SUITES, ScanCommand.TLS_1_3_CIPHER_SUITES, ScanCommand.HTTP_HEADERS, } )
# Queue scan scanner.queue_scans([scan_request])
# Get results for result in scanner.get_results(): print(f"Scan results for {result.server_location.hostname}:")
# Check certificate cert_result = result.scan_result.certificate_info if cert_result.result: cert = cert_result.result.certificate_deployments[0] print(f" Certificate: {cert.received_certificate_chain[0].subject}") print(f" Valid until: {cert.received_certificate_chain[0].not_valid_after}")
# Check TLS 1.3 support tls13_result = result.scan_result.tls_1_3_cipher_suites if tls13_result.result: print(f" TLS 1.3 supported: {len(tls13_result.result.accepted_cipher_suites)} ciphers")
# Check HSTS headers_result = result.scan_result.http_headers if headers_result.result: hsts = headers_result.result.strict_transport_security_header print(f" HSTS enabled: {hsts is not None}")
if __name__ == "__main__": scan_endpoint("api.example.com")

best_practices.practice: Use SSLyze for programmatic TLS validation
Integrate into Python-based CI/CD pipelines
Combine with testssl.sh for comprehensive coverage
Store results in structured format for analysis
